summary: Recorded for the 2020 election, Robert Evans and Cody Johnston read three more chapters of Ben Shapiro's 2016 novel True Allegiance, mocking its prose and its plot that treats racial profiling as heroic and an Obama-like president as a villain.

evidence.note: Hosts resume reading True Allegiance as an election-day special
Novel frames community policing in Detroit as a sinister plot; hosts call it racist
Prosecutor declines to charge the officer who killed a Black teenager
Bridge bombing used to justify the war on terror in the novel
Hero demands customs files on Arab-looking men; long critique of racial profiling
Muslim friend serves as an FBI informant in mosques; novel laments end of mosque monitoring
Villain president redirects troops to rebuild infrastructure, framed as evil

notes: Middle instalment of the multi-episode True Allegiance reading; Katy Stoll absent this time. Time is the novel's 2016 publication and its near-present fictional setting (approximate); the 2020 election is only the recording context. No theme fits right-wing polemical fiction exactly; propaganda-media chosen to match sibling records. Detroit (MI) and New York (NY) share the setting, so no single subdivision.
